en: The Root Mantra of Santānagopāla.
Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ glauṃ! O son of Devakī, Govinda, Vāsudeva, Lord of the Universe!
Grant me a son, O Kṛṣṇa; I have come to you for refuge.
Oṃ, salutations to the Blessed One Vāsudeva.
[I offer praise] to Hari, the protector of the lineage, the auspicious one, whose eyes are like lotus petals, the delight of Devakī.
I bow to Kṛṣṇa, the slayer of Madhu, for the attainment of the sacred teachings. ||1||
I bow to Hari, Vāsudeva, the protector of cows, the delight of Nanda, the child resting on Yaśodā’s lap, for the sake of obtaining a son. 2.
For the sake of obtaining a son for us, I always bow down to Govinda, who is praised by sages, to Vāsudeva, the delight of Devakī. (3)
I bow to Gopāla, to the child-like one, to Acyuta, the Lord of Kamalā;
for the sake of obtaining a son, I salute Kṛṣṇa, the preeminent of the Yadus. 4.
I bow to the lotus-eyed Lord of Kamalā, the son of Devakī, who bestows the fruit of the Putrakāmeṣṭi sacrifice, for the sake of my obtaining a son. (5)
O Lord of Lakṣmī, O lotus-eyed one, O lotus-navelled Janārdana!
Grant me a son, O Śrīśa, Vāsudeva, Lord of the Universe! 6.
I bow to Govinda, the infallible Lord of Śrī, who rests upon the lap of Yaśodā, who is the child praised by sages, and who is the source of the attainment of our sons. 7.
O Lord of Śrī, O God of gods, O Acyuta who removes the suffering of the distressed!
O Govinda, grant me a son; I bow to you, O Janārdana. (8)
O Govinda, who grants the desires of devotees, protect your devotee, O bestower of auspiciousness!
O Lord Kṛṣṇa, beloved of Rukmiṇī, grant me a son. (9)
O Lord of Rukmiṇī, Sovereign of All, grant me a son forever;
O Lotus-eyed One, who is a wish-fulfilling tree for devotees, I have come to you for refuge. (10)
O son of Devakī, O Govinda, O Vāsudeva, O Lord of the Universe!
Grant me a son, O Kṛṣṇa; I have come to you for refuge. (11)
O Vāsudeva, adored by the world, Lord of Śrī, Supreme Person!
O Kṛṣṇa, grant me a son; I have come to you for refuge. (12)
O lotus-eyed one, O Lord of Kamalā, O supreme among the supremely compassionate!
Grant me my son, O Kṛṣṇa; I have come to you for refuge. (13)
O Lord of Lakṣmī, O Padmanābha, O Mukunda, O you who are praised by sages!
Grant me a son, O Kṛṣṇa; I have come to you for refuge. (14)
I always bow to you, Vāsudeva, who are the nature of cause and effect;
I bow to you, the wise one, the bestower of happiness, for the sake of obtaining a son. 15.
O lotus-eyed Śrī Rāma, enemy of Rāvaṇa, Hari, Poet!
I bow to you, O Lord of Gods; grant me a son, O Hari. (16)
O Lord of the Universe, I worship you for the sake of obtaining a son;
grant me a child, O Kṛṣṇa, Vāsudeva, Lord of Ramā! (17)
O Kṛṣṇa, Vāsudeva, Lord of the Universe, you who steal the pride of proud women and who stripped the gopīs of their garments, grant me my son! 18.
O delight of the Yadus, O Lord of Ramā, Vāsudeva, Mukunda, praised by sages, grant us the attainment of a son! (19)
O Vāsudeva, grant me a son; O Mādhava, grant me a child.
O Śrī Kṛṣṇa, give me a son; O Great Lord, give me a calf. (20)
O Śrī Kṛṣṇa, grant me a child; O Rāghava, grant me a son.
O Aśoka-tree for your devotees, O delighter of the Nanda family, grant me a son. (21)
O Kṛṣṇa, Vāsudeva, Lord of the Universe! O Kamalanātha, Govinda, Mukunda, who art adored by the sages! Grant me joy. (22)
Otherwise, there is no refuge; you alone are my refuge.
Grant me a son, grant me prosperity, and bestow upon me a son who is the very embodiment of prosperity.
For the sake of obtaining a son, I eternally worship Hari, the joy of the Yadus, who has tawny eyes and who, though knowing how to drink the breast-milk of Yaśodā, was himself drinking it. 24.
O delighter of Nanda, Lord of gods, grant me a son, O Lord;
O Consort of Ramā, Vāsudeva, Lord of the universe, grant me a son endowed with prosperity.
"O Mādhava, grant me a son who is prosperity, and prosperity that is a son;
O Lord of Śrī, take heed of our words of distress. (26)
O Gopāla, O Child, O Govinda, O Vāsudeva, O Lord of Ramā!
Grant us a child, and grant us prosperity, O Lord of the World! (27)
O Acyuta, son of Devakī, grant me the fruit of my desire;
O delight of the Yadus, fulfill this blessed prayer for a son. (28)
I entreat you, O Śrī Rāma, wish-fulfilling gem for devotees, desire-granting tree, great Lord: grant me a son; bestow upon me the wealth of a child. (29)
O delight of the Raghus, grant me always your own son, a joy, a child, a youth, an infant, a little boy, a progeny, and an offspring. (30)
I bow to Mādhava, the protector of the lineage, the granter of the desires of his devotees—the eternal Govinda—for the sake of obtaining a son for us. (31)
I bow to the leader of the Yadus, the son of Devakī, who is joined with the syllable Oṃ, who is Gopāla, who is endowed with Śrī, the delighter of the Yadus, and who is joined with Klīṃ. 32.
O Vāsudeva, Mukunda, Lord of lords, Govinda, Mādhava, Acyuta!
O Kṛṣṇa, Lord of Ramā, Great Master, grant me a son.
O lotus-eyed Govinda, O Kapilākṣa, O Hari, O Lord!
O granter of all desired boons, grant me a son forever. (34)
O Lord of the Universe, who resembles a blue lotus and the form of a multitude of lotuses;
O Mādhava, leader of Ramā, grant me an excellent son. (35)
O Nandapāla, O Dharāpāla, O Govinda, O delight of the Yadus!
O Kṛṣṇa, O Lord, beloved of Rukmiṇī, grant me a son. (36)
O Dāsa, Mandāra, Govinda, Mukunda, Mādhava, Acyuta, Gopāla, Puṇḍarīkākṣa! Grant me a son and prosperity. (37)
O Leader of the Yadus, O Lord of Padmā, O Son of Nanda’s wife!
Grant me my child, O Kṛṣṇa, O Śrīdhara, O Lord of my life! 38.
Grant us our desire; grant us a son, O Lord of Ramā!
O Blessed One, Kṛṣṇa, Sovereign of all, Vāsudeva, Lord of the universe! (39)
O beloved of Satyabhāmā, who are the essence of the heart of Ramā;
O Lord Kṛṣṇa, lover of Rukmiṇī, grant me a son. 40.
O Moon-and-Sun-eyed one, Govinda, Lotus-eyed one, Mādhava!
O God, Lord of the World, grant us a virtuous son through our good fortune. (41)
O lotus-eyed one whose form is compassion, worshipped by Padmanābha, grant me a son, O Kṛṣṇa, the delighter of Devakī! 42.
O son of Devakī, O Śrīnātha, O Vāsudeva, O Lord of the universe, O bestower of the fruits of all desires, grant me a son forever. (43)
O Śaṅkara, O Acyuta, O Mādhava, you who are as profound as the wish-fulfilling tree for devotees; O Lord of Śrī, who are affectionate toward cowherd boys, grant me a son. 44.
O Lord of Śrī, O Sovereign of Vāsudeva, O Delight of Devakī’s heart!
O Mandāra tree for devotees, O Lord of the worlds, grant me a son. (45)
O Lord of the Universe, O Lord of Ramā, O Lord of the Earth, O Ocean of Compassion!
O Vāsudeva, O Lord of All, O Master, grant me a son. 46.
O Śrīnātha, lotus-petal-eyed Vāsudeva, Lord of the World!
Grant me a son, O Kṛṣṇa; I have come to you for refuge. (47)
O Govinda, who is like a celestial mandāra tree to the servant and a wish-fulfilling gem to devotees, O Lord Kṛṣṇa, grant me a son; I have come to You for refuge. (48)
O Govinda, lotus-eyed one, Lord of Ramā, Great Master!
O Kṛṣṇa, grant me my son; I have come to you for refuge. (49)
O Śrīnātha, lotus-petal-eyed Govinda, Madhusūdana!
O Janārdana, I worship you for the sake of attaining the fruit of a son for my son.
I bow to Mukunda, who rests upon the lap of Yaśodā; he gazes with a gentle smile at his mother’s lotus-face while drinking her milk, his radiant limbs touching her other breast with his fingers.
I beg you for a lineage of sons, O lotus-eyed one! Grant me a son, O Kṛṣṇa; I have come to you for refuge. (52)
O Lord of the World, I am anxious for the attainment of sons;
O one adored by sages, grant me quickly that which is to be given by you. (53)
O Vāsudeva, Lord of the World, Consort of Śrī, Supreme Person!
O Kṛṣṇa, worshipped by the Lord of the Gods, grant me the boon of a son. 54.
Make me one whose son is granted by you, O beloved delight of Yaśodā;
and, O Hari, a lineage of sons must be bestowed upon me by you.
O Vāsudeva, Lord of the World, Govinda, Son of Devakī!
Grant me a son, O Rāma, the one who delights Kauśalyā. (56)
O lotus-eyed Govinda, O Viṣṇu, Vāmana, Mādhava!
O Rāghava, the lord of Sītā’s life, grant me a son. (57)
O lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa, adorned by the lord of gods, saluted by sages;
O Śrī Rāma, elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa, grant me a son forever. (58)
Give me back my son, O Rāma, the beloved delight of Daśaratha;
O leader of Sītā, lotus-eyed one, bestower of boons upon Mucukunda! 59.
O Mādhava, just as Laṅkā was formerly given by you to Vibhīṣaṇa, grant us a son in that same manner.
I contemplate your lotus feet without interruption.
O Rāghava, beloved as life to Sītā, grant me back my son. 61.
O Rāma, bestower of desired boons, granter of the fruit of obtaining a son;
O Lord of Śrī, saluted by the lotus-seated Brahmā, grant me a son. 62.
O Rāma, O Rāghava, O Lord of Sītā, O younger brother of Lakṣmaṇa, grant me a line of sons born of fortunate women; O beloved son of Daśaratha, grant me a son, O Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Gopāla, Mādhava! (64)
O Kṛṣṇa, Mādhava, Govinda, Vāmana, Acyuta, Śaṅkara!
O Lord of Śrī, leader of the cowherd boys, grant me a son. (65)
O cowherd boy, O most blessed one, O Govinda, Acyuta, Mādhava!
O Kṛṣṇa, Vāsudeva, Lord of the Universe, grant me a son. (66)
May this son of Devakī grant, may he grant a son; may he swiftly grant the attainment of a fortunate son.
May the Lord of Śrī, Rāghava Rāmacandra, swiftly grant, may he swiftly grant it.
May he grant, may he grant a son for the sake of expanding the lineage. || 67 ||
"Let my beloved son, the prince Nandana, who is always the leader of Sītā, be given to me by Vāsudeva. (68)
O Rāma, O Rāghava, O Govinda, O son of Devakī, O Mādhava!
Grant me a son, O Lord of Śrī, O leader of the cowherd boys! (69)
O Madhusūdana, grant me a son who shall expand my lineage;
give me a son, give me a son! I have come to you for refuge. (70)
O enemy of Kaṃsa, O Mādhava, O Acyuta, grant me my desired son!
Grant me a son, grant me a son; I have come to you for refuge. (71)
O Mādhava, grant me a son who shall endure until the end of the kalpa of the moon and sun;
grant me a son, grant me a son! I have come to you for refuge. (72)
O Lord Kṛṣṇa, son of Devakī, grant me always a son who is learned, intelligent, and illustrious. 73.
I bow to you, O lotus-eyed one, the granter of desires for the attainment of the netherworld (Sutala)—to Mukunda, the lotus-eyed Govinda, the slayer of Madhu. (74)
O Blessed One, Kṛṣṇa, Govinda, bestower of the fruits of all desires! Grant me a son, O Lord; I have come to you for refuge. (75)
O Lord, O Blessed One Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Mādhava, bestower of desires!
Grant me an eternal son; I have come to you for refuge. (76)
O Govinda, O lotus-eyed Lord of Kamalā, grant me a son!
Grant me a son, grant me a son; I have come to you for refuge. (77)
O Lord of Lakṣmī, O lotus-eyed one, O Pradyumna, O progenitor, O Master!
Grant me a son, grant me a son; I have come to you for refuge. (78)
O Lord of Ramā, who holds the conch, discus, mace, sword, and Śārṅga bow in Your hands!
O Kṛṣṇa, grant me a son; I have come to You for refuge. (79)
O Nārāyaṇa, Lord of Ramā, whose eyes are like lotus petals;
O Lord of Gods, worshipped by the lotus-like Padmā, grant me a son. (80)
O Rāma, O Rāghava, O Govinda, O delighter of Devakī! O Lord of Rukmiṇī, O Sovereign of all, O you who are worshipped by Nārada and the other gods! || 81 ||
O son of Devakī, O Govinda, O Vāsudeva, O Lord of the Universe!
O Śrīśa, O leader of the cowherd boys, grant me a son.
O Lord Govinda, worshipped by sages, beloved of Rukmiṇī!
O Kṛṣṇa, grant me a son; I have come to you for refuge. 83.
O Kṛṣṇa, whose mind is attached to the honey of the lotuses gathered by the cowherd girls, grant me my son; I have come to you for refuge. (84)
O Mādhava, who fulfills desires and whose heart is like a lotus pond agitated by waves, grant me my desired son; I have come to you for refuge. (85)
O Vāsudeva, Lord of Ramā, bestower of auspiciousness upon Your servants!
O Kṛṣṇa, grant me a son; I have come to You for refuge. (86)
O bestower of auspiciousness, Govinda, Murāri, saluted by sages!
O Kṛṣṇa, grant me a son; I have come to you for refuge. (87)
O bestower of sons, O Lord Mukunda, O beloved of Rukmiṇī, O Master!
Grant me a son, O Kṛṣṇa; I have come to you for refuge. (88)
O lotus-eyed one, O Govinda, O Vāsudeva, O Lord of the World!
Grant me my son, O Kṛṣṇa; I have come to you for refuge. (89)
O Vāsudeva, ocean of mercy, Mukunda, adored by sages!
O Kṛṣṇa, grant me a son; I have come to you for refuge. (90)
We always pay homage to Govinda, worshipped by the gods, the bestower of the perfection of sons, to Kṛṣṇa, who grants the attainment of children. (91)
Salutations to you, the ocean of compassion, the beloved of the cowherd girls, the enemy of Mura! For the sake of obtaining a son, O All-pervading Lord, grant me a child.
Salutations to You, O Lord of Ramā, the beloved of Rukmiṇī;
grant me a son, O Śrīśa, the leader of the cowherd boys. (93)
Salutations to you, O Vāsudeva, who eternally desires Śrī; to the giver of sons, who reclines upon the king of serpents, and who reclines upon the stage. || 94 ||
O You who recline upon the couch of the earth, O Lord of Ramā, O bestower of auspiciousness, O Mādhava!
O Śrīśa, O leader of the cowherd boys, grant me a son. (95)
O Rāghava, bestower of mandāra flowers, grant a son to me, your wretched servant;
grant me a son, grant me a son, grant me a son, O Lord of Ramā! (96)
O Kṛṣṇa, you who are ever intent on granting the desired sons to Yaśodā’s daughter, grant me a son; I have come to you for refuge. (97)
O my chosen deity Govinda, Vāsudeva, Janārdana!
O Kṛṣṇa, grant me a son; I have come to you for refuge. (98)
O Lord of Creatures, O Blessed One worshipped by Vāsudeva and Indra, through your grace may my son be possessed of moral conduct, wealth, and learning. (99)
Whoever recites this "Hymn of a Hundred Sons" shall also possess virtuous sons;
this jewel of a hymn, spoken by the illustrious Vāsudeva, leads to happiness. (100)
One who recites this daily at the time of chanting shall obtain sons, wealth, prosperity, sovereignty, and the honor of kings immediately; of this there is no doubt. (101)
